quandoUsar: Show live what an agent is doing on a long task: each step has a type (`search`, `read`, `write`, `think`, `run`) that picks the icon.
Steps that collect short findings, such as files, sites or results: they appear as chips, one by one, as the `items` list grows.
Runs with many steps, where finished steps should fold into a single line with a count and total time, and reopen on demand.
quandoEvitar: Use `todo-list` when the whole plan is known from the start and you only need to mark each step as pending, in progress or done.
Use `tool-result` when you need to show the full input and output of each tool call.
Use `loading-states` for a short wait, with no steps to list.

teclado.acao: With focus on the summary line, opens or closes the list of finished steps.
Moves focus to the summary line, the component's only control; it exists only after the first step finishes.

acessibilidade: The root is a `<section>` with `aria-label` equal to `title`; the summary is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`, and the collapsed list is `inert`.
An invisible `role="status"` region announces the title of the running step and, at the end, how many steps finished; pending and failed steps get a screen-reader-only suffix.
The fixed texts (“steps finished”, “Done”, “(waiting)”, “(failed)”) are in English in the code and have no translation prop.
movimento: On the running step, a ring pulses around the icon and a shimmer runs across the title; chips enter one by one with a short spring, without overshoot.
When a step finishes, it leaves the live list and folds into the summary line with a height spring, while the finished count rolls to the new value.
With “reduce motion” on, the pulse, shimmer and spin stop, heights change instantly and chips appear without animation.
responsivo: Fills 100% of the parent's width: the header and each step's `detail` truncate with an ellipsis on one line, while the step title and chips wrap.
notasIA: It is data-driven: pass `steps` with a stable `id` and update `status` (`pending`, `running`, `done`, `error`), `items` and `duration` while the agent works; the component does not measure time itself.
Each text in `items` is used as the chip's `key`: do not repeat the same text within a step.
Finished steps start collapsed; use `defaultExpanded` or the `expanded` and `onExpandedChange` pair to open them, for example when a step ends with `error`.
